facts.statement: Jixiangornis lacked teeth like later avialans but retained a long tail unlike modern birds.
facts.quote: Like later avialans, it had no teeth, but it also had a long tail, unlike modern birds.

facts.statement: Jixiangornis had a long forelimb measuring 131% of its hindlimb length, suggesting it possessed some aerial ability.
facts.quote: The long forelimb (131% of hindlimb length) indicates at least some aerial ability.

facts.statement: Jixiangornis is known from only one complete but juvenile fossil specimen.
facts.quote: Jixiangornis is currently known only from a single specimen, a complete but juvenile skeleton.

facts.statement: The Jixiangornis fossil was discovered in the Yixian Formation near Beipiao City in western Liaoning, China.
facts.quote: The fossil was found in the Yixian Formation near Beipiao City, western Liaoning, China.

facts.statement: Studies by Hartman et al. (2019), Cau (2020), and Wang et al. (2020) concluded Jixiangornis was a member of the family Jeholornithidae but not a synonym of Jeholornis.
facts.quote: Hartman et al. (2019), Cau (2020) and Wang et al (2020) found Jixiangornis to have been a jeholornithid but not a synonym of Jeholornis.

facts.statement: Jixiangornis lived between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago during the Barremian to Aptian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 119.57 million years ago)
